summary: McKean County, PA 60-ft steel Blaw-Knox tower on the McDade farm near Kane, built 1923, burned cabin 1944, removed before 1994; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: steel Blaw-Knox tower, 60 ft (18.3 m), set on a concrete foundation
facts.status_note: Removed before 1994 per FFLOS; a November 1944 fire destroyed the cabin and equipment and a rebuild was reported as planned; no source describes the site now

staffing.status: ranger or fire warden in charge, named in 1928, 1932 and 1944 items

events.note: Built on the H.C. McDade farm about two miles from Kane; FFLOS gives 1923; foundation work began late September 1923
Youths wrecked the phone line by sliding horseshoes down the wire while the ranger was away (April 19, 1928 item)
Warden LeRoy Horton spotted a blaze in the Cook Forest area southwest of Kane (April 21, 1932 item)
Observer at the tower spotted a fire near Altoona, 125 miles away (May 26, 1932 item)
Blaze of undetermined origin destroyed the cabin and equipment atop the tower (November 2, 1944 item); rebuilding reported as planned
FFLOS: removed before 1994; the year is an upper bound, not a date
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives one build year, 1923, and no rebuild. A November 1944 item says the cabin and equipment burned and that rebuilding was to start at once. The story keeps 1923 as the build year and reports the planned rebuild without saying it happened.

notes_for_editor: Brief lat/lon 41.6772, -78.7633 is not in FFLOS, which lists no coordinates; left unverified and not corrected. The 1964 survey description is the only account of the site location; it is a 1964 description, not a current one. Ownership and access today not established. The word 'Removed' on the Forest Lookouts page sits above a survey record and reads as a page label. Brief height 18.3 m matches 60 ft in the 1923 items.
